questions.question: If water reaches 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure, it ___ rapidly.
questions.explanation: Ye ek permanent physical aur scientific law hai. Zero Conditional (Type 0) mein condition aur result dono hamesha Simple Present mein rehte hain: 'If + Simple Present, Simple Present'. Isliye subject 'it' ke sath singular verb 'boils' (A) sahi hai. 'Will boil' (B) specific future prediction ke liye use hota hai, jo universal facts par lagu nahi hota.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Universal truths aur permanent scientific cause-and-effect relationships mein dono clauses Simple Present (V1/V_s/es) mein rehte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the advocate submits the certified copy by 4 PM, the court clerk ___ the urgent listing today.
questions.explanation: If-clause Simple Present ('submits') mein hai aur future realistic event ('by 4 PM today') ki shart rakhta hai. First Conditional (Type 1) formula ke mutabiq result clause mein 'will + V1' lagta hai: 'If + Simple Present, will + V1'. Isliye 'will prepare' (B) correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Realistic future conditions mein result clause 'will / shall + V1' demand karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the High Court ___ the notification tomorrow, thousands of candidates will download their admit cards.
questions.explanation: Result clause 'will download' First Conditional structure banata hai. English syntax mein conditional if-clause ke andar future time hone ke bawajood 'will' use nahi hota; wahan Simple Present ('releases') lagta hai. 'Will release' (A) common Indian English trap hai jo grammatically galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Conditional clauses (if, unless) mein future time express karne ke liye Simple Present (V1/V_s/es) use hota hai, 'will' nahi.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the junior engineer knew the administrative password, he ___ the database server right now.
questions.explanation: If-clause Simple Past ('knew') mein hai aur present imaginary situation ('right now') ko express karta hai (reality ye hai ki use password nahi pata). Second Conditional formula ke hisaab se result clause mein 'would + V1' lagta hai: 'would restart' (B). 'Would have restarted' (C) past unreal (Type 3) ke liye hota hai jo 'right now' ke sath match nahi karta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Present hypothetical/contrary-to-fact situation mein: 'If + Simple Past (V2), would + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If he ___ the District Magistrate, he would initiate strict disciplinary action against the corrupt contractor.
questions.explanation: Ye ek hypothetical contrary-to-fact condition hai (wo DM nahi hai). Formal English aur competitive exams mein singular subjects (he, she, I) ke sath bhi hypothetical condition mein strictly subjunctive 'were' (C) use hota hai. 'Was' (B) informal speech mein sunne ko milta hai lekin written exam standard par incorrect mana jata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Hypothetical present conditions mein sabhi persons ke sath subjunctive 'were' lagta hai: 'If + Subject + were ..., would + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the police department ___ the forensic report to the court last week, the judge would have granted bail to the applicant.
questions.explanation: Result clause 'would have granted' past counterfactual result dikhata hai (jo actually past mein nahi hua). Third Conditional formula ke mutabiq if-clause mein Past Perfect ('had + V3') lagta hai: 'If + had + V3, would have + V3'. Isliye 'had submitted' (C) correct answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Unreal past situations mein if-clause Past Perfect ('had + V3') leta hai aur result clause 'would have + V3' leta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically CORRECT according to standard conditional rules?

options.text: If the driver would have applied the brakes earlier, the collision would have been averted.
If the driver had applied the brakes earlier, the collision would have been averted.
If the driver had applied the brakes earlier, the collision would be averted.
If the driver applied the brakes earlier, the collision will be averted.

questions.explanation: Option B standard Third Conditional structure ('If + had applied, would have been averted') ko perfectly follow karta hai. Option A mein fatal error hai: if-clause ke andar 'would have' lagaya gaya hai. Option C mein conditional mismatch hai (Type 3 condition ke sath Type 2 result bina kisi present time reference ke). Option D mein tense discord hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06 & PIT-01: If-clause ke andar 'would' ya 'would have' ka use strictly prohibited hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: ___ the administrative officer informed the candidates in advance, they would not have faced this procedural delay.
questions.explanation: Sentence formal inverted conditional structure mein hai jisme 'if' omit kar diya gaya hai. Main verb V3 'informed' hai aur result clause 'would not have faced' hai. Type 3 inversion ka formula hota hai: 'Had + Subject + V3 ..., Subject + would have + V3'. Isliye 'Had' (C) sahi answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Type 3 Inversion formula: 'Had + Subject + V3 ..., would have + V3'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: ___ you encounter any authentication error while logging into the High Court portal, contact the system administrator.
questions.explanation: Ye Type 1 First Conditional ki formal inverted form hai ('If you should encounter' ➔ 'Should you encounter'). Yahan base verb V1 'encounter' hai aur result clause imperative command 'contact' hai. Formal conditional inversion mein contingency ke liye 'Should' (B) lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Type 1 Inversion formula: 'Should + Subject + V1 ..., will / imperative'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Unless the applicant ___ the original certificates before the scrutiny committee, his candidature will be cancelled.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' ka matlab hota hai 'if not'. Isliye unless wale clause mein doosra negative word 'does not' (A) lagane se double negative error banta hai. Conditional conjunction hone ke kaaran 'will' (C) bhi nahi lag sakta. Isliye 3rd person singular subject ke sath affirmative Simple Present 'produces' (B) hi correct answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & PIT-04: 'Unless' clause hamesha affirmative form mein rehta hai; isme 'not' lagana double negative banata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the candidate had completed the specialized database course last year, he ___ as a Senior System Assistant today.
questions.explanation: Ye ek Mixed Conditional hai: Condition past ki hai ('had completed last year'), lekin result aaj present moment ka ongoing state hai ('today'). Standard Type 3 mein result past ka hota hai ('would have worked'), lekin yahan 'today' ke kaaran result present hypothetical form 'would be working' (B) mein aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Mixed Conditional (Past Condition ➔ Present Result): 'If + Past Perfect, Subject + would + V1 / would be V-ing (today/now)'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If you fulfill all the eligibility criteria prescribed in the official advertisement, you ___ for the post of System Assistant.
questions.explanation: If-clause Simple Present ('fulfill') mein hai. Result clause mein eligibility ke basis par permission ya ability dikhane ke liye present modal 'can apply' (A) perfectly suitable hai. 'Could apply' (B) hypothetical Type 2 ke liye hota hai, jabki yahan real possibility ki baat ho rahi hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: First Conditional mein result clause certainty ('will') ke alawa ability ('can') ya permission ('may') bhi express kar sakta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03
